work: A3/A6 — root-cause of the HTTP 422 seen in a36_verify_mine.json

inputs.task: open wikipedia and find information about charminar

observation.dashboardSurfaced: Agent reasoning failed: Backend agent endpoint failed: HTTP 422

rootCause.explanation: The uvicorn serving port 8010 had etimes=13935s (~3.9h) and was launched WITHOUT --reload. It had been started before the A3/A6 backend change landed, so the in-memory AgentContextPayload still lacked `decision_state`. AgentContextPayload inherits StrictModel with extra='forbid', so a payload carrying the newly added field was rejected before any provider call. This is an environmental staleness artifact, NOT a defect in the A3/A6 payload contract and NOT a weakened schema.

proofs.claim: The current working-tree AgentContextPayload ACCEPTS a payload carrying decision_state.
git HEAD backend/app/models.py does NOT contain decision_state at all, which is exactly why the stale process rejected it.
extra='forbid' is intact: a genuinely unknown field is still rejected by the current model.
proofs.observed: unknown field still rejected: True -> totally_unknown_field

proofs.claim: After restarting the backend, the live OpenAPI schema advertises decision_state and still forbids additional properties.
The identical real request now passes schema validation and fails only at the provider.
proofs.interpretation: 422 is gone. The request is accepted by the model layer; the run now terminates at the provider. This is a real behavioural change observed in real Chrome against the real backend, not inferred.
